source.title: The Triangle of Similarity: A Multi-Faceted Framework for Comparing Neural Network Representations

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity across model families and compares CKA with Procrustes. Its reported family clusters and metric disagreements refine the scope of broad similarity claims, but it does not test similarity increasing with scale.
record.gate_note: The study reports static inter-model similarity patterns on CIFAR-10 and CKA–Procrustes agreement/disagreement. It does not sweep model scale or capability, compare paired image and caption representations, or test feature sharing across seeds, mappings, or recurring interpretable features. Its pruning results primarily compare each model with its own pruned version, so they do not measure the claim's cross-model convergence.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-model representational similarity (CKA, Procrustes) across CNNs, ViTs and VLM vision encoders. It reports low cross-family similarity, bearing on V7's incompleteness, and CKA–Procrustes disagreement in 4 of 21 pairs, bearing on V6's metric dependence. There is no scale sweep, image–caption pairing, seed analysis, mapping or feature-level test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that architectural families form distinct representational clusters and that CKA and Procrustes can disagree, so multiple views are needed. They also conclude that task accuracy is more brittle under pruning than representational structure, and that static similarity correlates strongly with robustness under sparsity (r = 0.882). Pruning may reveal a shared core for some pairs. They present the framework as an initial baseline.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses CKA and Procrustes within a broader framework that also includes functional and pruning analyses; it does not reproduce a scale-dependent convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported cross-model similarity pattern is assessed with both CKA and Procrustes; the authors report significant divergence between these metrics for 4 of 21 pairs. Static comparisons use CIFAR-10, while the cross-view analysis uses ImageNetV2, but the text does not report a direct comparison of input-dataset effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Architecture family, not training objective or data, is reported as the primary predictor of similarity. DINOv2, CLIP, BLIP and the LLaVA vision tower cluster tightly with supervised ViT/DeiT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity across vision models is driven mainly by shared architecture (self-attention vs convolution) rather than shared objective or data.

fits_no_version.finding: Under global magnitude pruning, cross-model similarity (e.g., ResNet18 vs ResNet50) stays stable or rises at moderate sparsity. Cross-family pairs show non-monotonic curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning can expose a shared computational core, increasing cross-model similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Static similarity of a pair correlates with robustness of its similarity under sparsity (Pearson r = 0.882, 21 pairs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pairs that are more similar at rest keep their similarity better under pruning.

record.problems: No numeric pairwise similarity values are given in the text for the architectural clusters. The metric-disagreement summary has an internal count inconsistency: it reports 4 of 21 pairs as divergent but says the other 20 pairs were standard. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the cluster or disagreement results.
record.rows_left_out: Pruning findings about CKA self-similarity and accuracy, LMC barriers, the static-similarity/robustness correlation, and qualitative cross-model similarity changes under pruning are omitted because they concern self-versus-pruned models or other relationships, not the claim versions' cross-model convergence, scale trend, or metric/data dependence.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no trend of alignment with model size or performance.
No image–caption paired representation comparison; only VLM vision towers on images.
Random-init and different-dataset ResNet variants are listed, but no seed-to-seed feature or subspace result is reported.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired alignment test.
No neuron, SAE-feature or circuit recurrence test.
No variation of metric hyperparameters such as neighbour count. No direct side-by-side static comparison of in-distribution versus OOD inputs.
No plateau-with-scale test. No test of whether shared data or objectives explain alignment.

missing.what: Stated robustness of architectural clustering on OOD (CIFAR-10) inputs, relevant to V6's data-dependence part.
Cross-family pairs vs within-family pairs under pruning (non-monotonic cross-model similarity; possible rise at extreme sparsity).
missing.locator: The Triangle of Similarity in Practice, Case 1 and Case 2

record.verdict_notes: Short workshop-style preprint with qualitative heatmap claims and few numbers. The record's '4 vs 20' inconsistency stems from conflating the metric-disagreement count with the static-vs-robustness 'Standard' classification. The V6 data-dependence challenge is weak because no in-distribution static comparison is shown.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, nor comparison of independently trained models' alignment as they become larger or more capable.
No paired image-caption representation comparison or test of alignment changing with vision- and language-model performance.
Although randomly initialized variants are listed among the models, no result tests shared features or subspaces across training seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.

The study compares CKA and Procrustes, but does not vary neighbour count or other metric settings. Static similarity is reported on CIFAR-10; the text does not compare the same static analysis across input datasets or report a systematic in-distribution versus out-of-distribution change.

The study reports incomplete similarity across architectural families, but does not test a plateau with scale or whether shared training data/objectives rather than a common model of reality explain the similarities.

rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise layer representations using CKA and Procrustes.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10 test set; 5,000 images upscaled to model resolution
ResNet18/50 variants, ViT-Tiny-Patch16, DeiT-Tiny-Patch16, DINOv2-Base, CLIP-ViT-B/32, BLIP-ViT-B/16, and LLaVA-1.5-7B vision tower

rows.value: High similarity within CNNs and within Transformers; cross-family similarity remains low. The text describes the CNN cluster as less tight than the Transformer-based cluster.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative description of the heatmaps; no pairwise numerical scores are provided in the text. The authors identify architectural family as the primary predictor of similarity.
rows.check: Qualitative heatmap description only; no numeric pairwise scores. It bears on V7's incompleteness part only, not on the cause part.

rows.value: The metrics are described as highly correlated; the text says all other 20 pairs exhibited “Standard” patterns.
rows.note: The study gives no numerical correlation for CKA versus Procrustes. Its statement that 4 of 21 pairs diverged leaves an arithmetic inconsistency with the statement that the other 20 pairs were standard.
rows.check: Value mixes two findings. The 'other 20 pairs Standard' sentence refers to static-vs-sparsity-robustness consistency, not CKA–Procrustes agreement, so the arithmetic inconsistency is likely a misreading. The value should be: CKA and Procrustes 'highly correlated' (Figure 5 bottom), with no numeric correlation given.
